label: make + appointment
sentence: I need to ___ an appointment with the dentist before the end of the week.
explanation: 'make an appointment' es fijo. HOLD a meeting sí existe, pero no HOLD an appointment.

label: pay + attention
sentence: The teacher asked the whole class to ___ attention to the diagram on the board.
explanation: 'pay attention' es una colocación fija. GIVE attention existe pero suena forzado y no es lo que pide el examen.

label: make + impression
sentence: It is important to ___ a good impression at a job interview.
explanation: 'make an impression': la impresión se produce en el otro. MAKE.

label: keep + temper
sentence: Try to ___ your temper even when the customer is being completely unreasonable.
explanation: 'keep your temper' = no perder la calma. HOLD your tongue existe, pero temper va con KEEP.

label: spend + time + on
sentence: She ___ a great deal of time on that project before finally handing it in.
explanation: 'spend time ON something'. PASS time existe pero significa entretenerse, no dedicarle esfuerzo.

label: do + your best
sentence: She ___ her best to finish the report before the deadline on Friday.
explanation: 'do your best' es fijo. Ojo: en español decís 'hacer lo mejor', pero acá no va MAKE.

label: make + decision
sentence: After months of discussion they finally ___ a decision to move abroad.
explanation: 'make a decision': la decisión se PRODUCE, no se ejecuta. Por eso MAKE y no DO.

label: do + favour
sentence: He ___ me a favour by picking up the parcel on his way home from work.
explanation: 'do someone a favour' es fijo. DO se usa para tareas y servicios; MAKE, para crear o producir algo.

label: do + homework
sentence: You must ___ your homework before you watch any television tonight.
explanation: 'do homework': es una tarea asignada, no algo que creás. DO.

label: make + profit
sentence: The company ___ a huge profit last year despite the recession.
explanation: 'make a profit': la ganancia se genera. WIN es para competencias, no para dinero de una empresa.

label: fit = talle
sentence: This jacket doesn't ___ me; the shoulders are far too wide.
explanation: FIT es cuestión de TALLE. SUIT sería que no te queda bien de estilo o color.

label: suit = estilo
sentence: That colour really ___ you — you should wear it much more often.
explanation: SUIT es que te favorece. FIT sería solo el talle, que en un color no aplica.

label: lend vs borrow
sentence: Could you ___ me your bike for the afternoon? Mine has a flat tyre.
explanation: LEND es dar prestado; BORROW es pedir prestado. Acá se lo pedís a él, así que él LENDS.

label: say sin objeto
sentence: He ___ that he had never seen the man before in his life.
explanation: SAY va sin objeto de persona. TELL exigiría decir a quién.

label: tell + objeto
sentence: She ___ me that she would probably be late for the meeting.
explanation: TELL lleva objeto directo de persona: tell ME. SAY no puede: sería 'said TO me'.

label: it takes + tiempo
sentence: It ___ me two hours to get here this morning because of the traffic.
explanation: 'It takes someone + tiempo + to do something' es una estructura fija. LAST no entra en ese molde.

label: although + oración
sentence: The match went ahead exactly as planned ___ it was raining heavily.
explanation: ALTHOUGH introduce una oración con sujeto y verbo. DESPITE no puede.

label: despite + sustantivo
sentence: The match went ahead exactly as planned ___ the heavy rain.
explanation: DESPITE va seguido de sustantivo o gerundio. ALTHOUGH necesitaría una oración con verbo.

label: however entre punto y coma
sentence: The hotel was extremely expensive; ___, the service was absolutely excellent.
explanation: HOWEVER conecta dos oraciones independientes, con punto y coma o punto delante.

label: nevertheless
sentence: He worked extremely hard; ___, he failed the exam by just two marks.
explanation: NEVERTHELESS marca contraste. MOREOVER y BESIDES suman, THEREFORE concluye.

label: because of + sustantivo
sentence: The flight was cancelled ___ of the bad weather over the Atlantic.
explanation: 'because OF' + sustantivo. BECAUSE solo iría con una oración completa.

label: in case
sentence: You should take a coat ___ case it gets cold later this evening.
explanation: 'in case' expresa precaución y va seguido de presente, nunca de WILL.

label: so that
sentence: I took a taxi ___ that I would not be late for the interview.
explanation: 'so that' introduce propósito. 'such that' existe pero es otro registro y otro significado.

label: break down
sentence: The car ___ down on the motorway and we had to call for help.
explanation: 'break down' = averiarse un vehículo o una máquina.

label: look after
sentence: Could you ___ after my cat while I am away next week?
explanation: 'look after' = cuidar. CARE necesita FOR, no AFTER.

label: call off
sentence: The match was ___ off after the pitch flooded, and no new date was ever announced.
explanation: 'call off' = cancelar definitivamente. Ojo con 'put off', que sería posponer: acá nunca se reprogramó.

label: take off
sentence: The plane ___ off almost two hours late because of the storm over the Atlantic.
explanation: 'take off' = despegar. Es el phrasal fijo para aviones.

label: turn off
sentence: Remember to ___ off all the lights when you are the last one to leave.
explanation: 'turn off' = apagar un aparato. CLOSE the light es un calco del español que en inglés no existe.

label: come up with
sentence: He ___ up with a brilliant solution halfway through the meeting.
explanation: 'come up with' = ocurrírsele a uno una idea.

label: give up
sentence: She ___ up smoking three years ago and has never looked back since.
explanation: 'give up' = abandonar un hábito. TAKE UP es lo contrario: empezar uno.

label: put up with
sentence: I cannot ___ up with that noise from the building site any longer.
explanation: 'put up with' = tolerar. Es un phrasal de tres partes: se memoriza entero, no por piezas.

label: work out
sentence: We need to ___ out exactly how much the trip will cost before we book anything.
explanation: 'work out' = calcular o resolver.

label: good at
sentence: She is very good ___ explaining complicated ideas in simple language.
explanation: 'good AT something'. El calco de 'buena EN' lleva a IN.

label: apologise for
sentence: He apologised ___ arriving so late to the ceremony.
explanation: 'apologise FOR something'.

label: interested in
sentence: I am not really interested ___ football, to be completely honest with you.
explanation: 'interested IN' es fijo.

label: succeed in
sentence: She succeeded ___ persuading the whole committee to change its mind.
explanation: 'succeed IN doing something'. Después de la preposición va gerundio.

label: accuse of
sentence: They accused him ___ taking money from the company account.
explanation: 'accuse someone OF something'. Ojo: 'blame someone FOR' lleva otra preposición.

label: based on
sentence: The film was based ___ a true story that happened in the 1920s.
explanation: 'based ON' es fijo. En español decís 'basada EN', y ese calco es la trampa.

label: congratulations on
sentence: Congratulations ___ passing your driving test at the very first attempt.
explanation: 'congratulations ON something'. En español felicitás POR algo: otro calco.

label: depend on
sentence: The final result depends ___ how many people turn up on the day.
explanation: 'depend ON'. El calco de 'depender DE' lleva a poner OF, que está mal.

label: look forward to
sentence: I am really looking forward ___ seeing you again next summer.
explanation: 'look forward TO'. Ese TO es preposición, no infinitivo: le sigue gerundio.
